text:
alex: heads-up — CI perf alert for small-batch latencies on canary after last infra deploy (CUDA 13.2.1 + driver 552.2 + Triton 2.6.1). 95th jumped from ~45ms -> ~120ms for seq=128, bs=1/2. this is blocking the rollout :sob:

maria: seeing same on dedicated canaries. traces show kernel selection oscillation — different matmul kernel chosen between warm and cold runs. suspect autotune table flip after the driver bump.

chris: logs from a failed CI job: 
```
perf: latency_p95=121.3ms; tail spikes correlate with kv-cache misses and matmul_v2 kernel timeouts
kernel: matmul_v1  2.3ms | matmul_v2  12.8ms
prefetch: hit_rate dropped 92% -> 68% after deploy
```

jamie: can you paste the Triton autotune table snapshot? i want to confirm which kernel IDs are being preferred.

maria: pasted below from the failing job (seq=128, model=redwood-7b-quant):
```
autotune_table:
  - op=matmul, seq=128, batch=1 -> kernel_id: 0x7f23 (matmul_v2), score: 0.92
  - op=matmul, seq=128, batch=2 -> kernel_id: 0x1c9a (matmul_v1), score: 0.88
  - prefetch: policy=aggressive -> kv_shard=local
```

ryan: interesting — matmul_v2 performs worse on A100 for small batch/short sequence despite better microbench numbers on synthetic mats. sounds like memory access pattern plus driver scheduling change is hurting L2 prefetching for that kernel.

chris: ran a quick bisect locally narrowing to the infra driver bump: reverting driver 552.2 -> 551.4 restores p95 to ~48ms. so two suspects: driver or the Triton runtime change we pulled in the same deploy (we also upgraded Triton from 2.6.0 -> 2.6.1).

alex: can we reproduce in CI with matrix: {driver: 551.4, 552.2} x {triton: 2.6.0, 2.6.1}? I'll kick off jobs.

ci-bot: started job: perf-matrix/2315001234-01 (driver=551.4,triton=2.6.0)
ci-bot: started job: perf-matrix/2315001234-02 (driver=552.2,triton=2.6.0)
ci-bot: started job: perf-matrix/2315001234-03 (driver=551.4,triton=2.6.1)
ci-bot: started job: perf-matrix/2315001234-04 (driver=552.2,triton=2.6.1)

jamie: also note our KV cache prefetch logic switches shard affinity heuristics depending on kernel selection; if kernel_v2 has a different tiling it shifts prefetch sizing and can cause interleaved memcpys -> more L2 evictions.

infra-bot: job perf-matrix/2315001234-02 finished: p95=119.8ms; prefetch_hit=69%
infra-bot: job perf-matrix/2315001234-04 finished: p95=123.4ms; prefetch_hit=66%
infra-bot: job perf-matrix/2315001234-01 finished: p95=46.2ms; prefetch_hit=91%
infra-bot: job perf-matrix/2315001234-03 finished: p95=47.9ms; prefetch_hit=90%

maria: those results point to driver 552.2 as the root cause. triton patch doesn't change much here.

chris: created a minimal repro harness that repeatedly runs the attention+matmul kernels with seq=128, bs=1 while collecting cupti traces. differences show kernel dispatch ordering changed — memcpys moved earlier causing L2 thrash. snippet: 
```
cupti trace diff:
- memcpy H2D at t=12us -> launch matmul_v1
+ memcpy H2D at t=6us  -> launch matmul_v2
```

ryan: driver scheduler tweak probably changed stream ordering heuristics. we should escalate to NVIDIA if driver change regresses our production workloads.

alex: next steps I'm proposing:
- stop the current rollout (canary) and pin driver back to 551.4 for clusters running critical canaries (maria) :heavy_check_mark:
- open support case with NVIDIA, include cupti traces + autotune table + CI artifacts (chris) :point_right:
- short-term software mitigation: force kernel selection to prefer matmul_v1 for small-batch/seq<=128 via TRITON_KERNEL_OVERRIDES env var (jamie) :wrench:
- add an autotune safety check in runtime: if p95 increases >30% after new kernel chosen, fallback to previous kernel automatically (alex + chris) :memo:

jamie: I can push a hotfix to runtime that allows per-model kernel preference toggle. will do a canary with that while infra pins driver.

maria: pinning driver on canary now. ETA 15m. will post results.

infra-bot: canary cluster pinned to driver 551.4 (action by maria)

maria: quick canary run after pin: p95=49.1ms, prefetch_hit=90%. reverting driver fixed it for now.

chris: filing bug/issue with full triage: link: https://goto.redwood/issue/ENGRT-2315 — includes bisect, perf matrix, traces, and suggested mitigations. tagging nvidia support.

ryan: if NVIDIA confirms this is driver-introduced scheduling change, we need a longer-term plan: either detect driver versions with known pathological scheduling and auto-apply kernel overrides, or add microbench-based validation in our CI gating to catch these shifts earlier.

alex: agreed. also adding a perf-gate to our deploy pipeline to run a small batch of real inference samples and check p95 delta before allowing driver/triton upgrades. I'll draft the pipeline change.

chris: moving to block/hold the rollout until we have either driver fix or our kernel-safety in prod. marking this thread as rollout-blocker.

jamie: I'll open a PR for runtime hotfix (small, opt-in env var flag) and link it here when ready.

alex: thanks everyone. summary: driver 552.2 regressed small-batch latency via altered kernel dispatch -> L2 prefetch thrash; pinned driver to 551.4 on canaries, opened NVIDIA ticket, implementing short-term kernel override and longer term autotune safety checks. keeping this thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
